subject: Request: regional peering impact — temporary p95 SLO relief
messages:
From: Amanda Klein <amanda.klein@clarityhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary SLO relief for hosted API (p95) during backbone maintenance

Hi Jonas,

We have a scheduled regional backbone maintenance in our cloud provider (US-WEST) the week of June 10. Our SRE team has run the preflight and is expecting brief but elevated latency for HTTP calls transiting the peering fabric during the 00:00–06:00 UTC maintenance window on 2027-06-10.

We use Redwood’s hosted API for our inference layer (model pinned: open-llama-13b-v1) and rely on your p95 commitment in our contract. Given the anticipated transient queuing in the peering path, can we request a temporary, scoped SLO exception for p95 for that 6-hour window? Specifically: 1) a defined temporary p95 forgiveness threshold for US region, 2) agreed measurement window and evidence package, and 3) rollback/monitoring expectations.

I can share sample traces and a short CSV of tail latencies from our test runs — attaching them in my next message if useful. We’d like to avoid a formal procurement loop if possible and get a quick operational yes/no so our incident playbook can be updated.

Thanks — Amanda
Amanda Klein
Head of SRE, ClarityHealth
Amanda.Klein@clarityhealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Klein <amanda.klein@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO relief for hosted API (p95) during backbone maintenance

Hi Amanda — thanks for the heads up and the clear ask.

We can support a scoped, temporary adjustment but need to lock down the exact parameters. A few immediate items so we can scope this without involving legal procurement:

- Proposed scope: US region, host: hosted inference endpoints used by ClarityHealth (model and route tags).
- Proposed temporary p95: allow increase from 250ms -> 420ms for the 6-hour maintenance window on 2027-06-10 (UTC).
- Measurement: standard Redwood p95 calculation across the configured measurement epoch; we will exclude queued/batched warmup artifacts if they match the pattern in your evidence.
- Evidence: please attach the CSV traces and a short summary (network provider maintenance ticket, expected start/end).
- Monitoring & rollback: we’ll watch token-level latency and error rates; if we see error-rate regression (>0.5%) we’ll apply an immediate fallback to a lower-latency variant (quantized model) for traffic from ClarityHealth.

I’m attaching a short one-pager (peering-impact-summary.pdf) with the initial risk assessment and the temporary SLO wording we’d include in an addendum. If that looks good to you, Monica and I can draft a short email addendum for signatures that keeps this operational (no change to billing).

Thanks Jonas — attached is the csv with sampled tail latencies from our canary on the provider’s preflight (latency-sample-queries.csv). The provider maintenance ticket is MT-92218 (scheduled start: 2027-06-10T00:00:00Z, expected end: 2027-06-10T06:00:00Z). We simulated steady traffic at 12 qps for 3 hours and saw p95 climb to ~410ms in two of five runs. Error rates stayed flat.

Two asks from our side to make this workable for ops:
- Confirm the measurement clock you’ll use and the precise metric namespace (so we can align our dashboards).
- Confirm the mitigation plan you mentioned (which fallback model variant and how long you’d keep it pinned).

If you can send the addendum draft today, I can route it for a quick engineering approval and sign-off.

—Amanda

Date: 2027-05-25T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary SLO relief for hosted API (p95) during backbone maintenance — proposed operational addendum

Team — forwarding ClarityHealth’s request and their evidence. Quick summary and recommended operational wording below (please treat as time-sensitive; they want a go/no-go to update runbooks):

Summary: ClarityHealth requests a temporary p95 relaxation for US region during a single provider maintenance window (2027-06-10 00:00–06:00 UTC). Their canary shows p95 touching ~410ms (error rate stable).

Recommended operational addendum (editable):
- Scope: ClarityHealth account (HS-23104), Hosted API (US region) endpoints pinned to production model variant.
- Temporary p95 threshold: 420ms for measurement window 2027-06-10 00:00–06:00 UTC (UTC clock).
- Measurement: use Redwood hosted p95 metric over the declared epoch; standard sampling rules apply. Token-level latencies and request/response errors remain in-scope.
- Exclusions: transient client-side retries that match the attached sample pattern may be excluded after ops review.
- Mitigation: if request error-rate > 0.5% during the window, automatically route ClarityHealth traffic to the pinned fallback quantized variant (latency-target: p95 < 300ms) until error rates stabilize.
- Evidence package: ClarityHealth will provide canary traces and the provider maintenance ticket.
- Credits: no billing credit; this is an operational exception to be recorded in the account file.

Ask: Lauren/Karthik — can you sign off on the wording and confirm we can implement the fallback routing in the scheduled window? Monica — I’ll coordinate ops runbook updates and the monitoring dashboard links. Marissa — FYI from an account risk perspective (no legal change requested).

If everyone agrees, I’ll send the final one-paragraph addendum to Amanda for engineering approval and a quick reply.

Jonas
